$comment: Crops of the captures in sources/, published on the marketing site and in the documentation. Regenerate with `node tools/visual/crop.mjs`; check with `--check`. Each entry says WHY its box is the shape it is, because that is the part a reviewer cannot read off the pixels. Coordinates are in the source's own pixels, origin top-left, as an image viewer reports them.

figures.why: The section's claim is 'say what should happen, without writing code', and the thing that shows that is the rule dialog: event, conditions, actions. The rule list behind it and the settings sidebar are context the sentence beside the figure already gives, and at the 600px this is published at they cost the dialog a third of its scale.

The live counters and one week of conversation traffic. The page continues with two more heatmaps of the same shape; including them would halve the scale of the numbers to show the reader a third copy of a pattern they have already read.

The same crop as the English figure, mirrored: under `dir=rtl` the dialog opens against the left edge instead of the right. Same box, so the two pages publish the same picture at the same scale rather than one that happens to be bigger.
The Arabic counters and the same week of traffic. Mirrored from the English box for the same reason.

The channel sidebar and the conversation list, which is what 'every channel in one list' means: each row says who wrote and which channel it arrived on. The homepage HERO already publishes this same capture whole, and a page that shows one screenshot twice tells a reader the band is decoration -- so the showcase takes the half the hero is not about.
